summary: Verified env-driven CORS allowlist + admin login flow on local backend (http://localhost:8001). 7/7 pytest tests pass: /api/health OK, /api/config/public returns google_client_id from env, OPTIONS preflight from ALLOWED origin (https://fund-runner.preview.emergentagent.com) returns 200 with access-control-allow-origin echoing origin and access-control-allow-credentials: true; OPTIONS preflight from BLOCKED origin (https://evil-attacker.com) returns NO access-control-allow-origin header; POST /api/auth/login with allowed Origin returns 200 with CORS headers and sets access_token/refresh_token cookies; same POST with blocked Origin returns no CORS header; standard login flow works and cookies are set. CORS security model is functioning as designed.

minor.issue: Response body returns access JWT under key 'token' (not 'access_token' as noted in the review spec). Cookies are correctly named 'access_token'/'refresh_token'. This is a naming inconsistency between body and cookie — frontend must read body.token. Consider aliasing to 'access_token' in AuthResponse for clarity.

action_items: OPTIONAL: consider renaming AuthResponse.token -> access_token to match cookie naming and common conventions (documented as 'access_token' in review request). Non-blocking.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py CORS setup is correct: strict allowlist from CORS_ORIGINS env, allow_credentials=True, no wildcard — matches user requirement.
Body field 'token' vs cookie 'access_token' naming mismatch (minor).
seed_data_creation: None; admin user is seeded by backend on startup.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_cors_and_auth.py covers CORS allowlist + login. Run via `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_cors_and_auth.py`. All checks against http://localhost:8001 (not REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL). Admin credentials in /app/backend/.env.
rca of the issue: No bug — user-reported 'network error on login' was suspected CORS. Verified that current CORS config strictly enforces the env allowlist and correctly permits credentials for listed origins. If a user still sees network errors from the browser, root cause is likely that the browser origin is not present in CORS_ORIGINS (must be added to backend/.env, then restart backend).
